ephemeris.note: Built-in Moshier ephemeris; no Swiss Ephemeris data files (se*.se1) or JPL kernels are used.

conventions.time: jd_tt, jd_ut = swe.utc_to_jd(y,m,d,h,mi,s,GREG_CAL). jd_ut is UT1 = UTC (no UT1-UTC); jd_tt = jd_ut + delta-T with swisseph's leap-second table (37 s carried forward after 2017). delta_t_s = deltat_ex(jd_ut, FLG_MOSEPH)*86400.
conventions.angles: degrees; longitudes 0..360 east of the equinox; speeds in deg/day; distances in AU (AU/day).
conventions.ayanamsa: get_ayanamsa_ut(jd_ut): ayanamsa relative to the mean equinox ('without nutation'). get_ayanamsa_ex_ut(jd_ut, FLG_MOSEPH): relative to the true equinox of date; equals tropical minus sidereal longitude when FLG_SIDEREAL is used. Both evaluated at jd_ut after set_sid_mode(mode,0,0).
conventions.houses: swe.houses_ex(jd_ut, lat, lon, hsys, 0): tropical. ARMC = sidereal time at Greenwich (true equinox, with nutation) * 15 + lon; cusps are computed with the TRUE obliquity (mean + nutation in obliquity), recorded in 'obliquity.true_obliquity_deg' from calc_ut(jd_ut, ECL_NUT, FLG_MOSEPH). ascmc order: asc, mc, armc, vertex, equatorial asc, co-asc Koch, co-asc Munkasey, polar asc. pyswisseph raises swisseph.Error where the C library returns retc=-1 with Porphyry cusps (Placidus/Koch inside polar circles); recorded as 'error'.
conventions.positions: swe.calc(jd_tt, ipl, FLG_MOSEPH|FLG_SPEED): geocentric apparent (light-time, gravitational deflection, aberration), true ecliptic and equinox of date, tropical. xx = [lon, lat, dist_au, dlon, dlat, ddist].
conventions.sunrise: swe.rise_trans(jd0, SUN, rsmi, (lon, lat, 0), atpress=0 (->1013.25 mbar), attemp=0 (->15 C), FLG_MOSEPH); jd0 = 0h UT of the civil date; the first event after jd0 is returned. Default rsmi = CALC_RISE/CALC_SET: upper limb with refraction. |BIT_NO_REFRACTION: upper limb, geometric. |BIT_DISC_CENTER: centre with refraction. UTC via jdut1_to_utc and revjul (hour as decimal).
conventions.kp: swisseph has no KP sub-lord tables; section left empty.
